x: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of dry air, followed by oxygen (21%), argon (0.93%) and carbon dioxide (0.04%).
t: Recall the order of atmospheric gases.

x: Argon is about 0.93% of dry air, the third most abundant gas. 21% is oxygen and 0.04% carbon dioxide.
t: Discriminate close percentage figures.

x: The troposphere averages about 13 km, from about 8 km at the poles to 18 km at the equator.
t: Discriminate average from extreme heights.

x: The ozone layer lies mainly at about 15–35 km in the stratosphere.
t: Recall the height of each layer.

x: Option B is incorrect: water vapour is a variable gas, from 0 to 4% by place and time. Nitrogen, oxygen and argon are permanent gases.
t: Discriminate permanent from variable gases.

x: Both are true and R explains A: strong equatorial convection lifts air higher, so the tropopause sits at about 18 km there against 8 km at the poles.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true and R explains A: ozone absorbs ultraviolet rays and turns them into heat, so the stratosphere warms with height.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true and R explains A: water vapour, dust, most of the air's mass and convection all lie in the troposphere, so weather forms there.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The troposphere has weather, meteors burn in the mesosphere, the ionosphere reflects radio waves and the exosphere is the outer region, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the feature of each layer.

x: Nitrogen is the major constituent and a nutrient, oxygen supports respiration and burning, carbon dioxide serves photosynthesis and the greenhouse effect and ozone absorbs UV, giving a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii.
t: Recall the role of each gas.

x: Aurora Borealis is northern, Aurora Australis southern, the thermosphere has strong ionisation and auroras, and the ionosphere has charged particles, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall the features of the upper layers.

x: All four are correct: water vapour stays near the surface, ozone is in the stratosphere, hydrogen reaches higher than nitrogen and oxygen, and CO₂ stays below about 20 km.
t: Recall the height of each gas.

x: I, II and III are correct. IV is false because the exosphere has extremely low air density.
t: Check each layer for a reversed property.

x: Both are true: the early atmosphere was reducing with little free oxygen, while today's is mostly nitrogen and oxygen.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Three are variable gases: water vapour, carbon dioxide and ozone. Nitrogen is a permanent gas.
t: Discriminate permanent from variable gases.

x: Oxygen is about 21%, CO₂ about 0.04%, water vapour 0–4% and ozone a trace, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the share of each gas.

x: Oxygen is the second most abundant gas, CO₂ a variable greenhouse gas, water vapour highly variable and falling with height and ozone absorbs UV, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the role of each gas.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: argon being an inert gas does not explain the order of abundance.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: permanent gases keep near-constant proportions, while variable gases change with place and time.
t: Discriminate permanent from variable gases.

x: Neon, helium, xenon, hydrogen and krypton are all trace gases. Every other group includes a major or variable gas.
t: Discriminate trace from major gases.

x: All four are correct: water vapour gives humidity, clouds and precipitation and is a greenhouse gas.
t: Recall the role of water vapour.

x: Methane and nitrous oxide are greenhouse gases. Hydrogen, krypton, neon, helium and argon are not.
t: Discriminate greenhouse gases from inert gases.

x: The stratosphere (13–18 to 50 km) warms with height and holds ozone, the mesosphere (50–80 km) cools and burns meteors, the thermosphere warms sharply from 80 km and the exosphere is outermost, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the order and features of each layer.

x: Both are true: the troposphere is the lowest layer and the one where life exists.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All three are correct: temperature falls with height in the troposphere at the normal lapse rate of 6.5°C per km, about 1°C per 165 m.
t: Recall the normal lapse rate.

x: All three statements are correct: temperature is high near the surface, lower aloft and very low at the tropopause. "Only three" is all that is listed.
t: Count carefully and note option wording.

x: Both are true and the key takes R as explaining A: the tropopause is the boundary because it separates the stormy troposphere from the stable stratosphere.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: All five are correct: the stratosphere lies above the troposphere up to 50 km, holds ozone in its lower part, has little weather and suits jet aircraft.
t: Recall the features of the stratosphere.

x: All five are correct: the ozone layer is O₃, three oxygen atoms, in the stratosphere, absorbing harmful UV and protecting life.
t: Recall the features of the ozone layer.

x: All five are correct: the mesosphere lies above the stratosphere, cools with height, burns meteors, ends at the mesopause and is very cold.
t: Recall the features of the mesosphere.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: auroras occurring there does not explain radio communication; ionised layers reflecting radio waves does.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: The stratosphere holds ozone, the thermosphere has high temperatures, the ionosphere reflects radio and hosts auroras and the exosphere is where satellites orbit, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the feature of each layer.

x: Both are true and R explains A: solar particles excite atoms in the upper atmosphere, which then emit light as an aurora.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: the exosphere has mainly light gases such as hydrogen and helium and slowly merges with space.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All four are correct: the troposphere cools with height and has weather, the stratosphere warms and holds ozone, the mesosphere cools again and the thermosphere warms sharply.
t: Recall the order and features of each layer.

x: The exosphere stretches from the top of the thermosphere to the outer limit of the atmosphere. 50–80 km is the mesosphere and 13–50 km the stratosphere.
t: Recall the height of each layer.

x: The modern atmosphere is oxygen-rich, the early one had CO₂, CH₄, NH₃ and H₂O, the order of abundance is N₂ > O₂ > Ar > CO₂ and the permanent gases are N₂, O₂ and Ar, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Discriminate early from modern atmosphere.

x: Both are true and R explains A: because life and air interact, photosynthesis by early organisms filled the atmosphere with oxygen.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Both are true: the exosphere has no defined temperature trend and is linked to space, and oxygen and nitrogen reach far higher than carbon dioxide.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Dust particles act as condensation nuclei, aerosols scatter or absorb radiation, dust and moisture form clouds and dust levels affect transparency, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Recall the role of atmospheric dust.

x: All four are correct: the layers go troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, ionosphere; the troposphere averages 13 km and is thicker at the equator, and water vapour falls with height and toward the poles.
t: Recall the features of the troposphere.

x: Ozone is in the stratosphere, the ionosphere handles radio and auroras, satellites orbit in the outer region and the exosphere is linked to UV absorption in the key, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the feature of each layer.

x: The troposphere runs from the surface to about 8 km at the poles and 18 km at the equator, cools with height, holds weather and ends at the tropopause, giving a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the features of the troposphere.

x: Both are true: the thermosphere is strongly ionised, and the ionosphere reflects radio waves for long-distance communication.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All three are correct: CO₂ is a variable greenhouse gas, and the thermosphere lies above the mesosphere.
t: Check each statement separately.
